incidents.title: Multi-stage intrusion: Application Layer Protocol → Network Service Discovery → Remote Services → Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (C2 beaconing)

alerts.title: C2 beaconing to a rare host
Brute force followed by a successful login

en.summary: 7 alerts on 20 hosts between 04/11 09:40 and 08/11 23:58 form one multi-stage intrusion. 10.10.1.37 beacons to 45.77.163.120 every ~60 s (6614 connections, a destination no other host uses). 10.10.1.37 scanned 5 hosts / 1024 ports with 99% of probes unanswered. 10.10.1.37 also probed hosts slowly (~9 unanswered probes, ~9 internal hosts touched, ~6 distinct ports / 5 min), below the per-window scan rule; the anomaly model caught it. 10.10.1.37 used account admin11 over SMB to reach 16 hosts in 15 minutes; this account was never used from 10.10.1.37 before. 10.10.2.20 uploaded 0.73 GB to 103.97.125.18:8443 at 08/11 02:31, a destination never seen before.
attack_chain: 04/11 09:40 · 10.10.1.37 · T1071.001 · 10.10.1.37 beacons to 45.77.163.120 every ~60 s (6614 connections, a destination no other host uses).
05/11 14:05 · 10.10.1.37 · T1046 · 10.10.1.37 scanned 5 hosts / 1024 ports with 99% of probes unanswered.

05/11 16:00 · 10.10.1.37 · T1046 · 10.10.1.37 also probed hosts slowly (~9 unanswered probes, ~9 internal hosts touched, ~6 distinct ports / 5 min), below the per-window scan rule; the anomaly model caught it.
07/11 10:30 · 10.10.1.37 · T1021.002 · 10.10.1.37 used account admin11 over SMB to reach 16 hosts in 15 minutes; this account was never used from 10.10.1.37 before.
actions: Isolate 10.10.1.37 from the network and collect memory and disk images
Block 45.77.163.120 at the firewall, proxy and DNS resolver
Block 103.97.125.18 at the firewall, proxy and DNS resolver
Isolate 10.10.2.20 from the network and collect memory and disk images
Reset the password of 'admin11', revoke its sessions and review where it logged in
Check 16 hosts reached by admin11 for new services, scheduled tasks or admin-share files
Rotate credentials stored on 10.10.2.20 and identify the data that left
Search all hosts for connections to 45.77.163.120
Search all hosts for connections to 103.97.125.18

vi.summary: 7 cảnh báo trên 20 máy từ 04/11 09:40 đến 08/11 23:58 tạo thành một cuộc xâm nhập nhiều giai đoạn. 10.10.1.37 gọi về 45.77.163.120 khoảng mỗi 60 giây (6614 kết nối, đích không máy nào khác dùng). 10.10.1.37 quét 5 máy / 1024 cổng, 99% gói dò không được trả lời. 10.10.1.37 còn dò chậm (~9 gói dò không trả lời, ~9 máy nội bộ bị chạm, ~6 cổng khác nhau / 5 min), dưới ngưỡng của luật quét cổng; mô hình bất thường đã phát hiện. 10.10.1.37 dùng tài khoản admin11 qua SMB để vào 16 máy trong 15 phút; tài khoản này chưa từng dùng trên 10.10.1.37. 10.10.2.20 tải lên 0.73 GB tới 103.97.125.18:8443 lúc 08/11 02:31, một đích chưa từng thấy.
attack_chain: 04/11 09:40 · 10.10.1.37 · T1071.001 · 10.10.1.37 gọi về 45.77.163.120 khoảng mỗi 60 giây (6614 kết nối, đích không máy nào khác dùng).
05/11 14:05 · 10.10.1.37 · T1046 · 10.10.1.37 quét 5 máy / 1024 cổng, 99% gói dò không được trả lời.
05/11 16:00 · 10.10.1.37 · T1046 · 10.10.1.37 còn dò chậm (~9 gói dò không trả lời, ~9 máy nội bộ bị chạm, ~6 cổng khác nhau / 5 min), dưới ngưỡng của luật quét cổng; mô hình bất thường đã phát hiện.
07/11 10:30 · 10.10.1.37 · T1021.002 · 10.10.1.37 dùng tài khoản admin11 qua SMB để vào 16 máy trong 15 phút; tài khoản này chưa từng dùng trên 10.10.1.37.
actions: Cách ly 10.10.1.37 khỏi mạng, thu bản sao bộ nhớ và ổ đĩa
Chặn 45.77.163.120 trên firewall, proxy và DNS resolver
Chặn 103.97.125.18 trên firewall, proxy và DNS resolver
Cách ly 10.10.2.20 khỏi mạng, thu bản sao bộ nhớ và ổ đĩa
Đặt lại mật khẩu 'admin11', thu hồi phiên đăng nhập và rà soát nơi tài khoản đã đăng nhập
Kiểm tra 16 máy mà admin11 đã vào: dịch vụ mới, tác vụ lập lịch, file trên admin share
Thay toàn bộ thông tin đăng nhập lưu trên 10.10.2.20 và xác định dữ liệu đã bị lấy
Tìm kết nối tới 45.77.163.120 trên toàn bộ các máy
Tìm kết nối tới 103.97.125.18 trên toàn bộ các máy

en.summary: admin11 reached 9 hosts over SMB from 10.10.1.11 (ws11), a workstation this account normally uses, during office hours. This matches an IT software push, not stolen credentials.
actions: Match the activity to an IT change ticket, then allowlist software pushes from 10.10.1.11

actions: Confirm with the owner of 10.10.2.20 that 34.120.177.193 is their monitoring service, then allowlist this pair

attacks.name: C2 beaconing
attacks.note: Implant on ws37 calls home over HTTPS every ~60 s with 30% jitter.

attacks.name: Port scan (fast)
attacks.note: Full 1-1024 TCP scan of four servers in a few minutes.

attacks.name: Port scan (slow, low-and-slow)
attacks.note: One probe every ~34 s for two hours, below the per-window rule threshold.

attacks.name: SSH brute force with success
attacks.note: 420 failed SSH logins in ~20 min, then the 'deploy' account gets in.

attacks.name: Lateral movement over SMB
attacks.note: Stolen admin11 credentials used from a normal workstation to touch 16 hosts and db01.

attacks.name: DNS tunnelling
attacks.note: Long random TXT queries to one rare domain, about 15 per minute.

attacks.name: Exfiltration to rare external host
attacks.note: 0.73 GB leaves db01 at night to an IP never seen before.

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.summary: The adversary probes hosts for open ports and running services to choose next targets.
T1046.detection: Many destination ports or hosts from one source in a short time, mostly unanswered.
response: Confirm whether the source is an authorised scanner
Isolate the source if it is a user workstation
Review which services answered and patch or firewall them

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.summary: Repeated login attempts to guess passwords; a success after many failures means the account is likely compromised.
T1110.detection: Bursts of failed logins against one service, especially from the internet, followed by a success.
response: Disable or reset the account that logged in
Block the source IP at the edge
Require keys or MFA for SSH and remove password login
Review commands run in the session

T1021.002.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.summary: Valid (often stolen) credentials are used over SMB to reach other machines' admin shares.
T1021.002.detection: One account touching many hosts over 445 in minutes, from a host it does not normally use.
response: Reset the account's credentials and revoke sessions
Check the reached hosts for new services or scheduled tasks
Restrict admin accounts to admin workstations (tiering)

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1071.001.summary: Malware calls home over HTTP(S) at a regular rhythm to receive commands.
T1071.001.detection: Small, evenly spaced connections from one host to a rare external destination.
response: Block the destination at the proxy and firewall
Isolate the host and collect memory and disk
Hunt for the same destination across all hosts

T1071.004.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
T1071.004.summary: Data or commands are hidden in DNS queries, usually long random subdomains of one domain.
T1071.004.detection: Many unique, long, high-entropy subdomains of a single rare domain, often TXT records.
response: Sinkhole or block the domain at the resolver
Force clients to use internal resolvers only

T1048.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
T1048.summary: Large volumes of data are sent out to an attacker-controlled host.
T1048.detection: Unusually large outbound transfer, at an odd hour, to a destination never seen before.
response: Identify what data left and start breach notification steps
Rotate credentials stored on the source server
